- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, particularly if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 14-day EWMA or sentiment-weighted average to smooth out noise.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1 → -1 → +1), model often mispredicts direction; favor conservative mid-range forecasts.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is falling, model underestimates further drop; add 2–5% downward buffer for next 5 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75).
